title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This document is the canonical, company-wide reference for policies and core processes that affect all teams at Redwood Inference. It consolidates access & permission rules, change-management procedures, data handling requirements, procurement and expense workflows, vendor management expectations, travel policy highlights, and internal templates. Use this page as the first-stop reference and follow links to team-level runbooks or request templates when needed.

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: Provide a consistent, auditable set of policies and operational procedures that minimize security, compliance, and financial risk while enabling teams to move quickly.
- Scope: Applies to all employees, contractors, vendors, and interns at Redwood Inference, across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Specific requirements for regulated customers or private deployments may override sections and are called out in related pages.

Table of contents
-----------------
1. Access & permissions
2. Change management (infra & code)
3. Data management and classification
4. Procurement & expense policy
5. Vendor management
6. Travel policy summary
7. Internal templates and forms
8. Ownership, audits, and exceptions

1. Access & permissions
-----------------------
Intro: Access to systems and data is granted on a least-privilege, role-based basis. Requests, approvals, and periodic reviews must be auditable.

Key roles and responsibilities (high level):
- Resource owner: Owning team/service (must approve access requests for that resource).
- Identity & Access Management (IAM) team: configures and enforces access policies, performs quarterly reviews.
- Security team: reviews elevated access requests (e.g., production write, key material access).

Standard access types and examples:
- Read-only: telemetry dashboards, aggregated logs.
- Read/write: non-prod infrastructure, staging clusters.
- Production operator: can deploy, rollback, run ad-hoc jobs in production.
- Secrets/key access: KMS/HSM roles (requires additional approval and MFA).

Request and approval flow (numbered procedure):
1. Employee opens an access request via the Access Request form (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-form).
2. Request routes to resource owner for approval. If resource owner is unavailable, the team lead or on-call may approve temporarily (approval window = 48 hours).
3. For production write or secrets access, Security must provide secondary approval.
4. IAM team implements the role and logs the change in the access audit log.
5. Quarterly review: IAM sends review pull to owners; owners must re-approve or revoke access within 14 days.

Access expiry and service accounts:
- All temporary access must include an expiry (max 30 days without escalated approval).
- Service accounts: must be owned by a team and have a documented runbook; keys rotated every 90 days unless using short-lived credentials.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Break-glass procedures are documented in the oncall-and-incident-response runbook and require post-incident justification and audit entry within 24 hours.

2. Change management (infra & code)
--------------------------------
Goal: Minimize customer impact, ensure traceability, and enable safe rollouts for infra and code changes.

Change categories:
- Standard change: pre-approved, low-risk (e.g., minor infra scaling, routine config updates).
- Scheduled change: changes that affect production but are planned (require schedule and communication).
- Emergency change: unplanned work to restore service (requires after-the-fact review).

Required artifacts for changes:
- Change ticket (Jira) with: description, impact analysis, rollback plan, verification steps, owner, schedule, and affected services.
- For infra changes: Terraform plan, diff, and target workspace.
- For model-serving changes: model version, test-eval results, traffic-splitting strategy.

Change approval matrix (table):
| Change type | Approval required | Approver owner | Required lead time |
|-------------|-------------------|----------------|--------------------|
| Standard | Team lead | Service owner | 0-2 days |
| Scheduled (prod) | Eng Platform / SRE | Service owner + SRE reviewer | 48-72 hours |
| Security-sensitive | Security review | Security lead | 72 hours |
| Emergency | Post-facto review | Incident commander + Eng leads | N/A |

Deployment and rollback checklist (numbered):
1. Verify unit/integration tests and model/eval gating.
2. Ensure canary policy configured (default 5% for 30 minutes) or follow service-specific policy.
3. Monitor defined SLO metrics (latency P95, error rate) for 60 minutes post-deploy.
4. If metrics exceed thresholds, perform immediate rollback with documented reason.

Communication and windows:
- All production scheduled changes must be announced in #release-notifications and the company status page at least 48 hours prior.
- Maintenance windows: weekdays 01:00-04:00 UTC preferred for disruptive infra maintenance unless agreed otherwise.

3. Data management and classification
------------------------------------
Overview: Treat customer and internal data according to classification, retain minimal data needed, and ensure appropriate controls for storage, transit, and disposal.

Data classification levels:
- Public: non-sensitive marketing materials, published docs.
- Internal: internal company docs, tickets, non-customer logs.
- Restricted: customer PII, private deployment configurations, audit logs.
- Confidential: KMS keys, raw customer data for regulated customers, security incident details.

Handling rules by classification (table):
| Classification | Storage controls | Access controls | Retention |
|---------------|------------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Public | Any internal repo or public site | N/A | No limit |
| Internal | Internal docs, encrypted at rest | Role-based | 2 years default |
| Restricted | Encrypted storage (AES-256), VPC-restricted | Approval + MFA | 1 year default or customer contract |
| Confidential | HSM/KMS protected, restricted audit logs | Strict approval, monitored sessions | Per contract / security policy |

Data lifecycle and retention:
- Default retention: logs 90 days hot, 2 years cold; telemetry aggregated at 13 months.
- Deletion requests: People-ops and Security coordinate for employee data; Product & Legal manage customer deletion requests per contract and applicable laws.

Data handling checklist for projects that use customer data:
1. Confirm classification with Product and Legal.
2. Record intended usage and retention in the project data register.
3. Ensure encryption in transit (TLS1.2+) and at rest.
4. Use pseudonymization where possible for analytics.
5. Schedule a security review if accessing Restricted or Confidential data.

4. Procurement & expense policy
-------------------------------
Objectives: Control spend, ensure competitive sourcing, and enforce approval thresholds.

Purchase channels and thresholds:
- Low-value (<= $1,000): team lead approval, can use corporate card.
- Mid-value ($1,001- $25,000): finance approval required; use procurement request form.
- High-value (> $25,000): procurement + VP-level approval and three vendor quotes (unless sole-source justification).

Expense submissions (bulleted):
- Submit receipts and purpose within 14 days via the Expense system.
- Corporate card reconciliation must be completed monthly.
- Travel expenses follow the travel policy below; any exceptions require manager + finance sign-off.

Vendor contracting and PO process (numbered):
1. Initiate vendor evaluation with Procurement (procurement@redwood.ai).
2. Collect standard contract, security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ), and three bids for >$25k.
3. Legal reviews and signs vendor contract.
4. Finance issues PO and logs the vendor in the vendor registry.

5. Vendor management
--------------------
Goals: Ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and SLA requirements. Maintain vendor registry and conduct periodic reviews.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Security questionnaire completed (SIG/CAIQ or equivalent).
2. Contract contains appropriate data protection and liability clauses.
3. SLAs and support contacts are documented.
4. Vendor added to vendor registry with owner and renewal date.

Ongoing monitoring:
- Quarterly review for strategic or high-risk vendors.
- Annual security re-assessment for vendors with access to Restricted/Confidential data.
- Offboarding: revoke credentials and request certificate/key rotation when engagement ends.

Escalation matrix:
- Operational issues: vendor owner -> procurement -> legal.
- Security incidents: incident response -> security lead -> legal -> exec sponsor.

6. Travel policy (summary)
-------------------------
Purpose: Support business travel while controlling costs and ensuring traveler safety. Full travel policy (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/travel-policy) contains country/region-specific rules.

Key points:
- Book travel through the approved agency or self-serve with pre-approval for trips > $1,000.
- Class of travel: Economy for flights < 6 hours, Premium Economy for flights 6-10 hours with manager approval, Business for > 10 hours with VP approval.
- Per diem: meals and incidental allowances are defined per region (see travel policy doc).
- Insurance: company travel insurance covers business trips; register trips in the Travel Registry.

Emergency support and incident reporting:
- Traveler must contact People-ops and Security for emergency assistance.
- All incidents during travel must be logged within 48 hours.

7. Internal templates and forms
------------------------------
This section consolidates links and short examples for commonly used templates. Use the Canonical Templates folder for the latest versions.

Common templates (links & description):
- Access Request Form: for requesting RBAC or secrets access. (/confluence/templates/access-request-form)
- Change Request Template (Jira): includes rollback plan and verification steps. (/confluence/templates/change-request)
- Procurement Request Form: used to start vendor evaluations. (/confluence/templates/procurement-request)
- Vendor Risk Assessment: questionnaire template that vendors complete. (/confluence/templates/vendor-risk)
- Travel Authorization: pre-approval form for international travel. (/confluence/templates/travel-authorization)

Example: Change Request (Markdown snippet)
```
Summary: Update TF module to add autoscaler for inference-pool
Impact: Affects Dedicated inference workers in us-west-2 (expected 5% capacity change)
Rollback: Revert to previous TF module + taint nodes; rollback script: scripts/rollback.sh
Verification: P95 latency on model-x under 95th percentile baseline, e2e smoke tests passing
Owner: eng-platform/inference-ops
Schedule: 2026-11-01 02:00 UTC
```

Template governance:
- Templates are maintained in the Canonical Templates folder and require a template owner. Template changes must go through the standard change process if they alter compliance or financial workflows.

8. Ownership, audits, and exceptions
-----------------------------------
- Policy owner: People-ops (Asha Patel).
- Review cadence: Annual policy review; critical updates may be issued ad-hoc.
- Audits: IAM and Security conduct quarterly audits of access, Finance audits procurement and expense processes monthly.

Exceptions and risk acceptance:
1. Submit an Exceptions Request form (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/exception-request).
2. Provide business justification, compensating controls, and a proposed review cadence.
3. Exceptions are approved by the Policy Board (People-ops, Security, Legal, Finance) and recorded in the exceptions register.
